replies.text:
Step 2 checks:
- Automated abuse of reachable endpoints: design describes no sign-in, sign-up, or mail/SMS-sending form — only "The account settings page lets a logged-in user change their email address, phone number and shipping address"; no enumeration response or rate-limited surface is stated → not applicable (the single-reviewer enumeration threat assumes a uniqueness check the design never mentions).
- Staff/admin/moderator screens showing user-supplied content: design mentions no staff, support or moderation view → not applicable.
- Privileged actions with no record of who did it: profile change is instant and silent — "The change takes effect immediately without re-entering the password" → already covered by listed threat 8 (silent email change, repudiation).
- Personal/account pages browsers, proxies or CDNs could store: yes — "The account settings page lets a logged-in user change their email address, phone number and shipping address" is an account page rendering email, phone and shipping address → not covered by any listed threat.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV exports, emails or headers: design states no export, log view, or outbound mail → not applicable.
- Single-reviewer list: phone-number change as recovery/second-factor hijack is a distinct mechanism from the email/address threats and the design does state the phone number changes instantly → include, low-confidence but design-grounded.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-03",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["account settings page", "profile update endpoint", "session cookie"],
    "dataStores": ["user profile records"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["browser to application", "shared browser/proxy cache"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii", "credentials"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Account settings page with email, phone and address left in browser or proxy cache",
      "scenario": "The settings page renders the user's email, phone number and shipping address. With no cache restriction stated, a shared or kiosk browser keeps the rendered page in history and disk cache, and a shared corporate proxy may store it. Someone using the machine afterwards presses Back or opens the cache and reads the previous user's contact and shipping details without any session or credential.",
      "component": "Account settings page",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "one", "harm": "personal_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The account settings page lets a logged-in user change their email address, phone number and shipping address." },
        { "quote": "Sessions are kept in a cookie for 30 days." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-525"],
      "plainLanguage": "The page showing someone's email, phone and address can be saved by the browser or a shared proxy, so the next person at that computer can read it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Prevent caching of the account settings page",
        "given": "a response that contains the user's email, phone number or shipping address",
        "when": "the account settings page is returned to the browser",
        "then": "it is sent with no-store cache directives so browsers, shared proxies and CDNs do not retain it, and Back-button access after logout does not reveal the data"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Instant phone number change redirects SMS recovery and step-up codes to the attacker",
      "scenario": "The same form changes the phone number immediately with no password re-entry. An attacker holding a session (borrowed cookie, unattended browser) replaces the recovery phone with their own. Any SMS recovery code or step-up challenge afterwards reaches the attacker, so they retain access even after the legitimate owner resets the password, and the owner's own recovery path is broken.",
      "component": "Profile update endpoint (phone number field)",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "medium", "reach": "one", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "lets a logged-in user change their email address, phone number and shipping address" },
        { "quote": "The change takes effect immediately without re-entering the password." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V2.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-620"],
      "plainLanguage": "Swapping the phone number without a password lets an attacker take over the account's text-message recovery and keep access after a password reset.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Protect the recovery phone number",
        "given": "a signed-in session on the account settings page",
        "when": "the phone number is changed",
        "then": "the change requires password re-entry, is confirmed by a code sent to the old number, and the old number stays valid for recovery until the new one is verified"
      }
    }
  ]
}
